newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 1 PM.

text.p: * Politcians across the political spectrum expressed their opinions on the reform package unveiled last night by Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea.
- The measures are tough but vital to rid Romanian economy of its crisis, said Ion Diaconescu, leader of the Democratic Convention.
- The Democratic Party (PD) backs the government programme and sees it as the only alternative to avoid economic collapse, PD vice-president Bogdan Teodoriu said.
- The package presented by Ciorbea does not represent the only solution to speed up reform, said Teodor Melescanu, spokesman of the main opposition Party of Social Democracy.
He said the programme cannot be sustained by the current situation of the economy.

- National Unity Party leader Gheorghe Funar criticised the measures saying and slammed the government for what he called "turning Romania into a Euro-colony" by making it a pray for foreign investors and Western markets.
* Any process to expand NATO without Romania and Poland would be non-sensical, President Emil Constantinescu said in an interview.
* International Monetary Fund mission chief Poul Thomsen, gives news conference on contents of the government's reform and social protection programme.
* The cabinet holds meeting with local prefects to discuss steps to implement government policies and to fight corruption. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
